name: row statistics and affine
input: (2,3) matrix with distinct scales and shifts
test:
import torch
x = torch.tensor([[1., 3., 8.], [-4., 2., 5.]])
gamma = torch.tensor([2., -1., 0.5]); beta = torch.tensor([1., 3., -2.])

y = layer_norm(x, gamma, beta)
expected = torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(x, (3,), gamma, beta, eps=1e-5)
assert y.shape == x.shape and y.dtype == x.dtype
assert torch.allclose(y, expected, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
print('ok')

name: constant and single-feature rows
test:
import torch
for x in (torch.tensor([[5., 5.], [1., 1.001]]), torch.tensor([[7.], [-3.]])):
    gamma = torch.full((x.shape[-1],), 2.); beta = torch.full_like(gamma, -1.)
    y = layer_norm(x, gamma, beta, eps=0.25)
    expected = torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(x, (x.shape[-1],), gamma, beta, eps=0.25)
    assert torch.isfinite(y).all() and torch.allclose(y, expected, atol=1e-6)
print('ok')

name: float64 and unchanged inputs
test:
import torch
for x in (torch.tensor([[1., 4.], [-2., 8.], [3., 9.]], dtype=torch.float64).T, torch.tensor([[1., 4., 9.]], dtype=torch.float64)):
    gamma = torch.tensor([0.5, 2., -1.], dtype=x.dtype); beta = torch.tensor([1., -2., 3.], dtype=x.dtype)
    saved = [v.clone() for v in (x, gamma, beta)]
    y = layer_norm(x, gamma, beta, eps=0.02)
    expected = torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(x, (3,), gamma, beta, eps=0.02)
    assert y.shape == x.shape and y.dtype == x.dtype
    assert torch.allclose(y, expected, atol=1e-9, rtol=1e-7)
    for v, old in zip((x, gamma, beta), saved):
        assert torch.equal(v, old)
print('ok')
